items.title: The U.S.-Chinese-Russian Summit and the Future of Trilateral Nuclear Talks
items.summary:
U.S. President Donald Trump, who has sought nuclear arms control with Russia and China since his first term, may finally have his chance. The first-ever U.S.-Chinese-Russian leaders’ summit is set to take place in Shenzhen, with nuclear issues potentially on the agenda. Regardless of whether the summit yields substantive progress, it could make the prospect of trilateral nuclear arms control seem somewhat less remote than before. For Beijing, however, the summit’s symbolism matters most: Washington is finally treating its geopolitical and ideological adversaries as equals in addressing issues of global governance. items.title: Is China Misreading the Moment?
items.summary: When U.S. President Donald Trump lands in Shenzhen later this week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, he will sit down with Chinese leader Xi Jinping for the fourth time amid an unexpected détente between Washington and Beijing. The trade war of 2025 is in abeyance, the two governments have announced a relationship of “constructive strategic stability,” and, to the alarm of American allies, Trump and Xi are planning to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Beneath the surface, however, the détente is beginning to crack.
